items.headline: Auditor-General flags 136 lapses, including S$148m in MOH savings left undeclared
items.summary: The Auditor-General's FY2025/26 report raised 136 findings, among them the Health Ministry failing to declare S$147.96 million in project savings for seven years and 120 barred individuals entering the Marina Bay Sands and Resorts World Sentosa casinos despite exclusion orders.

items.headline: Coroner rules two Singapore teenagers died after making and inhaling their own meth
items.summary: State Coroner Adam Nakhoda found that a teenage boy and girl died in early 2025 with lethal methamphetamine levels after producing their own meth pills, ruling the deaths a misadventure from drug experimentation with no foul play. A gag order bars identifying them.

items.headline: British man convicted after assaulting a private-hire driver who died a year later
items.summary: Oruche Morgan Fidelis, 22, pleaded guilty to using criminal force on a 66-year-old private-hire driver at Sunset Way in June 2024; the driver fell, fractured his skull and died about a year later. Fidelis had earlier drunk several pints of beer.

items.headline: Singaporean man, 25, to be charged with murder over his girlfriend's death in Bali
items.summary: Indonesian police submitted the case to Denpasar prosecutors on July 17 to charge a 25-year-old Singaporean with murder over the death of his girlfriend in Bali, having identified the victim and completed forensic investigations.

items.headline: Police forcibly hospitalise activist Sonam Wangchuk after a 20-day hunger strike
items.summary: Police removed Sonam Wangchuk, 59, from Delhi's Jantar Mantar on July 18 and took him to Safdarjung Hospital, citing his deteriorating health on a fast begun June 28 to demand Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over exam-paper-leak allegations. His wife said he would keep fasting.

items.headline: India moves against youth protesters in Delhi ahead of the monsoon parliament session
items.summary: Authorities acted against demonstrators in New Delhi before protests over unemployment and alleged exam scams, as the movement piled pressure on Narendra Modi's government days before the monsoon session opens on July 20.

items.headline: HDFC Bank's June-quarter profit misses estimates as margins shrink
items.summary: India's largest private lender reported lower-than-expected first-quarter profit as net interest margins contracted, even with advances up 15.4% year-on-year; the miss weighed on bank stocks, which make up roughly 30% of the Nifty.

items.headline: Reliance beats profit estimates as strong refining offsets an Iran-war drag
items.summary: Reliance Industries' June-quarter net income fell 22% year-on-year to 209.5 billion rupees but beat the 198.23 billion analysts expected, helped by strong refining margins and growth in its consumer and technology arms.

items.headline: UK takes British Steel into full public ownership, ending Jingye's control
items.summary: The government nationalised British Steel on July 16 after the Steel Industry (Nationalisation) Act received Royal Assent, ending Chinese firm Jingye's ownership after rescue talks failed; ministers cited protecting domestic steelmaking and national security.

items.headline: Record 34 candidates to contest the Clacton by-election as Farage seeks a return
items.summary: A record 34 candidates were confirmed for the August 13 Clacton by-election, the most for a UK parliamentary seat, after Nigel Farage triggered it by resigning; rival main parties are boycotting the contest, whose field includes Count Binface and Laurence Fox.

items.headline: Burnham's path to No 10 is dogged by a policy vacuum and a Labour-left rebellion
items.summary: Days before Andy Burnham enters Downing Street on Monday, even allies describe a policy vacuum, indecision and a falling-out with a key ally, with the Labour left that helped install him already restive; he won nominations from 379 of Labour's 403 MPs.

items.headline: More than 2,700 UK deaths are linked to the May and June heatwaves
items.summary: Figures reported on July 13 linked over 2,700 excess deaths in England and Wales to the unprecedented May and June heatwaves, including about 2,200 between June 18 and 28, as England logged its warmest June since records began in 1884.

items.headline: Update: Two US troops killed and one missing in an Iranian strike on a Jordan base
items.summary: US Central Command said two American service members were killed and one is missing after Iranian ballistic missiles and drones struck the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan — the first US military deaths reported in the current round of fighting — with several others wounded.

items.headline: Update: Iran declares its US memorandum dead as strikes hit critical infrastructure
items.summary: Iran said the memorandum it signed with Washington last month is effectively suspended, with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei calling Trump's signature "worthless," as Tehran accused the US of striking critical infrastructure and reports put July's death toll near 50.

items.headline: Update: Ukrainian drones kill eight at Russian warehouses in the deadliest such strike in two years
items.summary: Ukrainian drone attacks killed at least eight people and wounded dozens at Wildberries logistics warehouses inside Russia on July 18, described as the deadliest Ukrainian strike inside Russia in two years, with Kyiv calling the sites sanctioned-component supply hubs.

items.headline: Magnitude 7.3 quake strikes off Mexico's Chiapas coast; tsunami alert later lifted
items.summary: A 7.3 earthquake struck off Chiapas in southern Mexico on July 17, briefly prompting a Pacific tsunami alert within 300km that was later lifted; it was felt in Guatemala and El Salvador, with only minor damage and injuries and no deaths reported.

items.headline: Databricks raises at a $188 billion valuation in a Coatue-led round
items.summary: Databricks is raising roughly $3 billion in a strategic round led by existing investor Coatue at a $188 billion valuation, up about 40% from its $134 billion mark in February; it plans to fund acquisitions and expand AI products including its Genie assistant.

items.headline: Microsoft preps Project Perception, a multi-model rival to Anthropic's security AI
items.summary: The Information reports Microsoft is preparing Project Perception, an AI security tool that scans code, cloud and endpoints for vulnerabilities and routes each task to Microsoft, OpenAI or Anthropic models to undercut the cost of Anthropic's Mythos.

items.headline: A $400 million loan uses AI inference chips as collateral in a first for the sector
items.summary: Inference-cloud startup General Compute secured a $400 million loan from investment firm Upper90 in what TechCrunch called the first debt deal backed by inference-specific chips, a sign financiers are shifting from training GPUs toward inference hardware.

items.headline: AI travel agency Fora reaches unicorn status with a $60 million Series D
items.summary: Fora, an AI-powered travel agency, raised a $60 million Series D led by Forerunner and Tactile Ventures at a $1 billion valuation, with Insight Partners and Thrive Capital joining, making the advisor-network startup a unicorn.

items.headline: Ex-DeepMind researcher raises $55 million at a $300 million valuation before any launch
items.summary: Andrew Dai, a former Google DeepMind researcher, raised about $55 million in seed funding at a $300 million valuation before shipping any product, choosing strategic backers Nvidia and Menlo Ventures over higher-valuation offers.

items.headline: Apple overtakes Nvidia as the world's most valuable company amid an AI rotation
items.summary: Apple briefly reclaimed the top spot Friday as Nvidia fell more than 3.5%, its market value reaching about $4.88 trillion against Nvidia's roughly $4.86 trillion — the first lead change since June 2025 — as investors rotated beyond the biggest AI winners.

items.headline: Gold heads for its biggest weekly loss in about six months as war revives inflation bets
items.summary: Gold held just below $4,000 an ounce Friday, near $3,965 spot, and was on track to lose more than 3% for the week — its steepest weekly drop since early June, per CNBC — as Middle East tensions lifted oil and rekindled rate-hike concerns.

items.headline: Abbott beats estimates and raises its 2026 profit forecast, shares jump 11%
items.summary: Abbott reported second-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.31 on 13% reported sales growth and lifted full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $5.45-$5.60, sending shares up almost 11% on strength in heart devices and diagnostics.

items.headline: ManpowerGroup surges 33% on an upbeat third-quarter revenue outlook
items.summary: ManpowerGroup jumped about 33% after guiding to third-quarter revenue growth of 2% to 6%, above the 1.7% consensus, making it a standout gainer in an otherwise weak session.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli beats Verstappen to pole for the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli took his sixth pole of 2026 with a 1:44.361 at Spa-Francorchamps, edging Max Verstappen by 0.317s; Lando Norris qualified third but starts 13th after a 10-place grid penalty, promoting George Russell.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli's title lead shrinks to 25 points over Russell heading into Spa
items.summary: Ahead of Sunday's Belgian Grand Prix, Antonelli's championship lead has narrowed to 25 points over Mercedes teammate George Russell, with Lewis Hamilton 32 back, after errors and misfortune trimmed his advantage across the last three rounds.

items.headline: 🏏 India and England meet at Lord's in a series-deciding third ODI
items.summary: The three-match ODI series is level 1-1 going into Sunday's decider at Lord's, with Washington Sundar ruled out by a leg injury and KL Rahul likely to return; the BCCI has said it will not be Rohit Sharma's final match.

items.headline: 🎾 Tsitsipas reaches his first final in 16 months at Gstaad
items.summary: Stefanos Tsitsipas beat Aleksandr Shevchenko to reach his first tour-level final since March 2025 at the Swiss Open Gstaad, where he will face Raphael Collignon, who upset Juan Manuel Cerundolo in the other semifinal.

items.headline: 🎾 Rublev sets up a Bastad final against defending champion Darderi
items.summary: Andrey Rublev beat Alejandro Tabilo 6-1, 6-2 to reach the Bastad final, where he meets defending champion Luciano Darderi, who edged Adolfo Daniel Vallejo 7-6(9), 6-4. The final is on Sunday.

items.headline: Hubble and Webb find the first of Omega Centauri's thousands of hidden black holes
items.summary: Astronomers detected oMEGACat BH-2, a 4.46-solar-mass black hole in the star cluster Omega Centauri whose companion star takes about 94 years to orbit it. Models predict roughly 10,000 such black holes hide in the cluster; this is the first confirmed.

items.headline: NASA's Psyche returns its first Mars flyby images and a time-lapse of the encounter
items.summary: NASA released data and a month-long time-lapse from Psyche's May 15 Mars gravity-assist flyby, which passed within 2,864 miles and imaged the 290-mile Huygens crater and the south polar ice cap, setting the metal-asteroid probe on course to reach 16 Psyche in 2029.

items.headline: A semaglutide trial reports the first human evidence a GLP-1 drug slows biological aging
items.summary: A UC San Diego randomised, placebo-controlled trial of 108 adults, published in Nature Communications, found semaglutide cut the pace of epigenetic aging by about 9% on the DunedinPACE clock over 32 weeks — the earliest human clinical hint the drug may affect aging beyond weight and metabolism.

items.headline: New spectra suggest Earth's quasi-moon Kamo'oalewa may not be lunar debris
items.summary: Webb and Large Binocular Telescope spectra taken in early 2026 look far less 'red' than earlier data, matching silicate asteroids rather than weathered Moon rock and pointing to a possible origin in the Flora asteroid family — complicating the leading theory as China's Tianwen-2 begins sampling the object.

fun_fact.headline: Astronauts grow taller in space
fun_fact.body: Astronauts come home from long missions measurably taller than when they left. In the near-weightlessness of orbit the spine is no longer compressed by gravity, so the discs between the vertebrae expand and an astronaut can gain up to about 3% in height — as much as 5cm on a tall crew member. The stretch is temporary: within a few months back on Earth, gravity squeezes the spine back to its normal length.

puzzle.title: The Painted Cube
puzzle.body:
A wooden cube measuring 3 × 3 × 3 is painted red on all six outer faces. It is then sliced with straight cuts into 27 identical unit cubes.

How many of the 27 small cubes end up with paint on exactly two of their faces?
puzzle.approach: Picture where a small cube must sit to show exactly two painted faces — corners show three, face-centres show one.
puzzle.answer:
12.

A small cube shows exactly two painted faces only when it sits along an edge of the big cube without being a corner. A cube has 12 edges, and on a 3×3×3 each edge holds exactly one middle cube between its two corners — so 12 small cubes have two painted faces.

Full tally: 8 corner cubes (three faces) + 12 edge cubes (two faces) + 6 face-centre cubes (one face) + 1 hidden core cube (no paint) = 27.

word_puzzle.title: Cornered
word_puzzle.body:
LETTER BOXED — three letters sit on each side of a square:

TOP:  W · H · R
RIGHT:  A · D · U
BOTTOM:  T · O · E
LEFT:  C · G · L

Rules: make words of three or more letters; each next letter must come from a DIFFERENT side; the following word must begin with the letter the previous word ended on; and together your words must use all 12 letters. Can you empty the box in just TWO words?
word_puzzle.approach: Trace a path around the box — each letter must jump to a different side, and the next word starts on the letter the last one ended on.
word_puzzle.answer:
WATCHDOG → GRUEL.

WATCHDOG runs W-A-T-C-H-D-O-G, with every letter on a different side from the one before it; GRUEL then starts on that final G: G-R-U-E-L. Between them the two words touch all twelve letters. (Each consecutive pair crosses to a different side of the box.)

notes: Singapore ran on Mothership (an allowed source): CNA and The Straits Times were unreachable from the routine environment, so the section skews to court/governance items; the AGO annual report (Jul 15) is the lead governance story.

India ran on fallback sources (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg): all six primary Indian outlets were unreachable and CNBC/SCMP surfaced no in-window India-domestic deep articles. Four verified items cleared (Wangchuk, pre-session crackdown, HDFC Bank, Reliance).

UK News ran on fallback sources (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg): BBC, Sky News and The Guardian were all egress-blocked (confirmed 403). British Steel led on the domestic nationalisation, not Beijing's protest. The heatwave-deaths item is dated by its Jul 13 report date.
Global carries three rolling-conflict Updates (Iran troop deaths, Iran memorandum collapse, Ukraine strike inside Russia), each with a concrete new development, plus the Mexico Chiapas earthquake.

Belgian Grand Prix at Spa confirmed as the current F1 round via Formula1.com; qualifying (Antonelli pole) ran Saturday, the race is Sunday ~21:00 SGT and had not run at publish time, so Sports carries qualifying and title-context items, not a race result.

Multiple retry attempts and fallback-tier searches were made per FIX 6 for the source-blocked sections (Singapore, India, UK); live web search was used for second-source verification of marquee items.

AP/Reuters deep URLs were not crawler-verifiable in this environment; Global items were sourced to reachable CNN/Al Jazeera deep links instead, and a Gaza Jul 18 item was dropped for lack of a verifiable allowed URL.
